learning_outcomes.text: Students gain knowledge of concepts and technologies necessary for building operating systems and knowledge of the modular structure and functionality of operating systems.
Students acquire knowledge and skills in the configuration, administration, and secure application of operating systems using commercial operating systems.
Students classify and evaluate modern operating forms of data centers, such as virtualization or cloud computing, in the context of operating systems.
Students gain insight into the theoretical foundations of a Linux system and an overview of the most important shell commands.
Students install and administer a Linux server.
Explain the importance of layered models and the tasks and functions of the layers of the ISO/OSI model, as well as the most important service representatives of each layer.
Reproduce the concepts of application protocols like HTTP and SMTP and understand their functionality, e.g., using sequence diagrams.
Program simple internet applications using sockets.
Analyze and diagnose network problems with suitable tools.

syllabus_topics: Dealing with Shells - graphical and text-based (especially practical use of the command line)
Use of system virtualization (e.g.: Hypervisors, VirtualBox, XEN, Docker, ...)
Network topologies (Bus, Tree, Star, partially/fully meshed)
Application layer: HTTP, SMTP & IMAP, DNS
Outlook on the network layer: IPv4/v6
Use of tools and techniques for network analysis and configuration (e.g., Ping, Traceroute, PuTTY/telnet, nslookup, ...)
Use of browser debugging tools (network console, ...)
Understanding and implementing text-based application protocols (e.g., HTTP interactions)
assessment_rules: The assessment is a 90-minute written examination. The weighting of the grade is 5/210.
